details.purpose: To record results from an audiological speech test conducted for the purpose of assessing speech recognition, speech discrimination and speech intelligibility.
details.use: Use to record the results of audiological speech tests carried out to assess the ability of a subject to understand speech in quiet or in noise, i.e. speech recognition, speech discrimination and speech intelligibility. Results can either be speech intelligibility scores for given stimulus levels (fixed SNR), or speech recognition thresholds obtained from adaptive procedures.
details.misuse:
Not to be used for audiological speech testing that is used for phonemic confusions analysis.
Not to be used to assess speech production.
Not to be used to record audiological speech tests where the presentaton level is not known - for example: unmonitored live voice.

items.items: Record of results from an audiological speech intelligibility test conducted for the purpose of assessing speech recognition, speech discrimination and speech intelligibility.
Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.
The obtained performance result (speech intelligibility in percent) for a test list, sentence or word presented at the given stimulus level.
Can be used for any speech intelligibility result in fixed or adaptive measurements.
The level of the varied stimulus.
Corresponds to speech or noise, depending on which level is varied during the measurement.
The obtained performance result in percent (speech intelligibility) at a given stimulus level.
The speech recognition threshold (or speech reception threshold; SRT) describing a speech level or signal-to-noise ratio required to reach the given target speech intelligibility.
The level of the speech stimulus required to achieve the target speech intelligibility in a measurement in quiet.
The level difference (signal-to-noise ratio; SNR) between the speech and noise stimulus required to achieve the target speech intelligibility in a measurement in noise.
Additional narrative about the speech intelligibility measurement not captured in other fields.
The type of noise stimulus used during speech in noise testing. Further details can be given in 'Noise type details'.
Not applicable for speech in quiet tests.
Noise that has the same power at all frequencies (i.e., a flat power spectrum).

Noise spectrum that approximates the average long term spectrum of adult male speech and has a slope below 100 Hz of +6 dB/octave, a flat spectrum between 100 Hz and 320 Hz, and above 320 Hz a slope of -6 dB/octave.
A recording of the voices of many people who are talking simultaneously, resulting in an unintelligible babble.
The masker is a single person speaking and this speaker is different to the speaker used for the test stimulus.
The voice type (sex) of the speech stimulus.
Stimuli presented by a female talker.
Stimuli presented by a male talker.
The mode used to enter or record the response.
The response is given by pointing to a picture of the stimulus item.
The response is given by pointing to written text corresponding to the stimulus item.
The type of the response set.
The type of speech stimulus used.
A consonant-vowel (CV) or CCV or VC or VCC item that is not a real word but is phonotactically correct.
Nonsense word comprising a consonant, then a vowel, then a final consonant, for example, "wub" or "yat".
A speech stimulus that is not a real word but is phonotactically correct.
A word comprised of a single syllable. For example, 'green'.
A word comprised of 2 syllables with equal stress on each syllable. For example, 'sunshine'.
A word that is comprised of two syllables with stress on the first syllable. For example 'bucket'.
The response is given by pointing to a 3-dimensional object.
The initial level stepsize for level changes after a response.
The initial presentation level of the stimulus varied during the measurement.
Speech level for measurements in quiet and varied stimulus level for measurements in noise.
The method used to present the speech test stimulus.
For example: a visual stimulus can be used to test lip reading skills.
An auditory stimulus is presented to the test subject.
A combination of auditory and visual stimuli are presented to the test subject.
A visual stimulus is presented to the test subject.
The type of announcement before presenting the speech stimulus.
An announcement sentence is presented prior to each stimulus.
A non-speech auditory announcement is presented prior to each stimulus (e.g., beep).
A visual cue is presented prior to each stimulus (e.g., flashing light).
No announcement prior to each stimulus.
The parameters of the adaptive test procedure.
The final level stepsize for level changes after a response.
The presentation level of the stimulus (speech or noise) fixed in level during the measurement.
Only applicable for speech in noise tests.
Sentence composed of a fixed syntactical structure without meaningful context.
A grammatical unit of one or more words that expresses an independent statement, question, request, command, exclamation, everyday-sentences etc.
Details on signals used as noise in 'Type of noise stimulus', e.g., name of established noise, number of talkers included in a babble noise, or other specific characteristics.
Not applicable for speech in quiet tests.
The name of the conducted speech test.

Use published name (including a reference) if possible.

Listener is native speaker in the presented test language.
Listener is fluent in the presented test language.
Listener has only basic proficiency in the presented test language.
Listener has no proficiency in the presented test language.
Details to explicitly record that this examination was not performed.
Information about hearing device use during the speech test.
Details of the hearing device used.
For example: hearing aid or cochlear implant as type of device.
Identification of the side where the hearing device is worn during the test.
The hearing device is worn at the left side.
The hearing device is worn at the right side.
Additional information about the hearing device that is not captured in "Hearing device" or "Side of hearing device".
For example: information about hearing device settings.
Additional issues or factors that may impact the speech test, not captured in other fields.
For example: medication or noise exposure prior to test.
The response is entered via a software interface.
The method used to present the test stimuli.
The stimulus is presented via a loudspeaker.
The stimulus is presented via insert earphones.
The stimulus is presented via external headphones - either circumaural or supraaural.
The stimulus is directly streamed to the sound processor of a hearing device.
Details of device used to present test stimulus as specified in 'Presentation method'.
For example: type of headphone or speaker.
The environment in which the speech test is administered.
Test environment that has been treated acoustically.
Test environment that has not been treated acoustically.
Room with free-field characteristics, also called 'anechoic room'.
For example: specific audiometric booth or a free text description of the room's sound treatment.
The language of the speech stimulus.
The target percentage of the speech intelligibility measurement.
Indicate for which stimulus (speech or noise) the level is kept constant during the measurement.
Only applicable for speech in noise tests.
The speech level is kept constant during the measurement.
The noise level is kept constant during the measurement.
Indicates if the measurement was performed for training or test purposes.
Applicable if the speech intelligibility test requires training, for example: Matrix test.

For example: mean of a certain numbers of reversals in an adaptive measurement, or psychometric function fit for several 'Measurements' at fixed levels.
Include reference if applicable.
The number of the used test list.

If applicable for the specific test, for example: Matrix sentence test or German monosyllabic speech test.
Specify in cluster 'Speech recognition threshold' if one test list is used in an adaptive measurement.
The number of the used test list.

If applicable for the specific test, for example: Matrix sentence test or German monosyllabic speech test.
Specify in cluster 'Measurement' if the SRT is calculated from several test lists presented at fixed level or SNR.
Stimuli presented by a synthetically generated female voice.
Stimuli presented by a synthetically generated male voice.
